toolArguments.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Asset: one complete seated player CHARACTER ONLY sprite, independently isolated on transparency.
Image 1 is the 3D CHARACTER-ONLY EDIT TARGET. It is a crude mesh scaffold for pose, nominal body scale, camera and seat contact. Replace primitive anatomy and crude shapes with a finished hand-painted RPG adventurer: natural face and ears, shaped dark brown hair with individual locks, expressive eyes, natural articulated hands, a tailored blue tunic with pale-blue edging and readable folds, a brown belt with small brass buckle, dark slate trousers and shaped brown leather boots with seams and soles. Refine the local silhouette and anatomy, hair, clothing and footwear into finished art, inside the same head-to-foot size and allotted frame. Do not merely texture the primitive forms.
Image 2 is the newly painted COMPLETE STOOL, SUPPORT AND STYLE REFERENCE ONLY. It establishes the same camera, warm painted materials and exact seat contact. Do not paint any part of the stool into the output. The edit target already has no stool, so create only the seated person; this is not stool erasure from a flattened image.
Preserve image 1's seated pose, facing, joint action, nominal anatomy scale, hand positions, pelvis contact and sole centers. The player is facing forward toward the viewer from above, sitting upright with bent thighs, knees and lower legs downward, arms relaxed alongside the thighs. Preserve nominal standing-height anatomy of 160 runtime pixels (1.25 of a 128px cell width); do not enlarge the head, body or shoes to show detail. Hair and clothing may refine edges within that existing scale.
Keep the entire 384x640 canvas of image 1, same subject placement/size and transparent margins. Runtime frame 192x320 and projected ground anchor (96,248), represented at double resolution. The seat support is 48 runtime pixels high; this elevation is already included in the target pose, so do not lift the person again. The pelvis attaches near runtime (96,220.48) and must align with the supplied stool when both full canvases are overlaid at their common ground anchor. Keep feet where the target places them.
Square-grid top-down oblique projection, front-facing three-quarter game view; fixed camera, screen-aligned ground, parallel projection, consistent top/front visibility, no perspective convergence or rotation.
Return one complete finished seated person only on genuine transparency, with all hair, hands and boots intact. No stool, seat, furniture, floor, ground shadow, background, checkerboard paint, labels or extra subjects.
